# P34.19 — Express-terms disclosure instead of withdrawal (A-8) + leak-taint withdrawal of 9 Atlas FR rows (F-337)

**Requirement ids:** **SIG-LIC-001**, **SIG-LIC-004**, **SIG-LIC-011**;
**SIG-GOV-007** (suppression for F-337) · findings closed: **F-403**
(closed by the ADR-183 acceptance + disclosure, not withdrawal),
**F-337** (nine leak-derived Atlas face-recognition rows leave every
public artifact) ·
**Base:** `r11/P34.16-public-repo-honesty-corrections-v2` (chain tip —
merge after it) ·
**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/219_P34.19__express-terms-disclosure.md`
(manifest row 219 — Round 11 / P34, sub-round 11A) ·
**Live stage:** **none** — repository fields, code and copy only; no
production mutation, no gate tick, no source flip. The disclosure
*renders* on pages via P34.17 (republish #1) and *ships in downloads*
via P34.21b (re-export, republish #2). The conditional API-side F-337
suppression got no in-ticket operator go → **D-P34.19-1** (owner
P34.46). `live_verification=false`.

## Why

ADR-183 records the operator's A-8 answers — **"Keep all, accept
risk"** and **"Keep everything as is"** — with the adopted sentence:

> I accept the express-terms risk for all ≈8,088 currently public rows, including the non-commercial ones; A-9 applies to new sources only.

plus the SB-2 clarification **"Yes, same sources (Recommended)"**:
scheduled refreshes of the same sources are covered; a new
non-commercial source follows A-9 (facts and pointers only). Until now
the ≈8,088 rows were public *without* disclosing the captured terms or
the acceptance basis (F-403); and nine Atlas face-recognition rows cite
the BuzzFeed News Clearview article whose agency data came from
"internal documents, which were uncovered by a source who declined to
be named" (I4-F103) — leak provenance, the same class
`wired_shotspotter_leak` is refused under (F-337, SIG-PUB-005).

## What this does

- **Disclosure is data, not code (SIG-LIC-004a).**
  `policy/src/policy/data/express_terms.json`
  (`sig.express-terms-disclosure/1`) carries the eight affected
  sources — `camreg_caloes_ca` (4,342), `camreg_cotgeo` (336),
  `camreg_keizer_or` (25), `camreg_ramallah_ps` (6), `camreg_und_023`
  (157), `camreg_trpa_us` (15), `camreg_ukm_my` (386),
  `camreg_txdot_rep_tx` (2,821) — with each source's captured terms
  **verbatim** (from the 2026-09-18 catalog sweep, evidence pointer per
  source), the basis `operator-accepted express terms (ADR-183)`, the
  ADR-183 accepted-sentence sha256
  (`cd76b74e…2fb4`), refresh scope (SB-2) and the code-computed public
  row counts (5,267 + 2,821 = 8,088 — computed from the release, never
  copied from the acceptance narrative).
- **`RightsRecord` gains three optional additive fields** —
  `captured_terms_verbatim`, `captured_terms_evidence`,
  `publication_basis` (default `""`; every prior fixture/caller keeps
  working). The eight `sources.toml` rights blocks carry the captured
  terms verbatim + basis; the registry loader parses them; the PG read
  store decorates the eight records from the committed policy table
  (read-only, additive — the DB rows predate the fields);
  `downstream_obligations()` emits the three keys for affected sources.
- **Withdrawals are a committed policy table, not scattered ids.**
  `policy/src/policy/data/publication_withdrawals.json`
  (`sig.publication-withdrawals/1`) names the nine F-337 upstream rows
  (AOS000953, AOS000960–966, AOS004507) with their entity + claim ids,
  the tainted locator, reason `leak-provenance` and the F-337/I4
  authority string. Miami carries **two** live FR claims bound to the
  same evidence captures and the upstream AOS row cannot be joined to a
  single claim from committed data — so `candidate_claim_ids`
  suppresses **fail-closed** alongside `claim_ids` until a host-side
  rerun narrows it (D-P34.19-1 names the join step).
- **The export drops the targets before any surface is built**
  (`build_spine_export`): matching claims out of `claims`, withdrawn
  entity ids out of `dataset.sites` and the map `exclude` set — so
  sites, record claims, tiles, search, dossiers, coverage, analytics
  and every derived artifact stay consistent. Each dropped claim is
  recorded loudly in `exclusions.json` (`withdrawn` array +
  `withdrawn_claims` total, reason + authority per row) — never a
  silent drop, never an `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on the spine.
- **The export emits the disclosure artifacts P34.17/P34.21b ride:**
  `web/terms_disclosure.json` (`sig.terms-disclosure/1` — every
  affected source the export actually carries, row counts computed from
  the built slices) and a per-compartment `ATTRIBUTION.json`
  (`sig.compartment-attribution/1`) wherever an affected compartment
  carries express-terms rows. Both land in the manifest with checksums.
- **The web data layer suppresses identically** — one shared
  `web/src/lib/withdrawals.ts` reads the SAME committed policy table
  (no second list) and `data.ts` filters every export-mode payload
  keyed on a suppressed claim/entity/upstream id (dossiers, map,
  watch, evidence, corrections, research queue, dossier index,
  entity compartments); `getTermsDisclosure()` reads
  `terms_disclosure.json` in export mode (missing = honest absence, an
  empty source list — never a fabricated entry) and a clearly-marked
  demo fixture in fixtures mode. Zero new client JS; static-first holds.
- **Copy batch #1** gains four `pending` SL-* rows (the interim
  sources-and-licences page's title, explainer, per-source basis line
  and refresh-scope sentence) — agent-drafted, sha256-pinned, shipping
  only on the operator's verbatim confirmation (B-2). The captured
  terms + basis are data, not drafted copy.
- **D-P34.19-1** records the owed hosted API-side suppression
  (read-only check 2026-10-03: all nine rows currently serve; the
  append-only `publication_disposition` write needs the operator's
  verbatim in-ticket go — owner P34.46, with `returnPass` rerun steps
  incl. the Miami narrowing join) plus its migration-anchor event.

## Tests

Every behaviour has a test that fails if removed:

- `tests/unit/test_express_terms_disclosure.py` (12) — the registry
  carries non-empty terms + basis on exactly the eight sources;
  verbatim equality with the policy table; basis/refresh-scope/accepted
  -sentence digest; `downstream_obligations` keys additive.
- `tests/unit/test_publication_withdrawals.py` (8) — the withdrawal
  table's nine entries, matching by claim id / candidate claim id /
  entity id, fail-closed Miami semantics.
- `tests/exports/test_p34_19_express_terms.py` (12) — the export
  fixture: 0 of the nine F-337 rows (claims, entities, sites, map,
  dossiers, search, exclusions-report `withdrawn` rows recorded
  loudly); `terms_disclosure.json` structure + slice-computed counts;
  per-compartment `ATTRIBUTION.json` contents.
- `web/tests/unit/withdrawals.test.ts` (5) +
  `web/tests/unit/terms-disclosure.test.ts` (3) — the shared filter
  drops every suppressed id class; the reader returns fixture/export
  payloads and honest absence.

## Boundaries

- No production mutation; no live leg; public `main` and the hosted
  API keep their state until the operator's merges/gos.
- No `ingestion_permitted` flip, no `HG-nn` tick, no spine
  `UPDATE`/`DELETE`; suppression is artifact-side, the spine records
  stay.
- `demo_*` pages, the interim sources page's build and the downloads
  re-export are P34.17's and P34.21a/b's — not claimed here.
- Diff budget: **over the ≤1,500 S ceiling — recorded, not smoothed.**
  2,250 changed lines excl. the generated current-projection
  (`docs/build/reports/current/`): tests 860, code 809, committed
  policy data tables 324 (verbatim terms + the nine-row withdrawal
  list), registry/batch/DEFERRALS/event 89, build records 219. The
  deliverables are atomic (a disclosure table is one artifact; the
  withdrawal table is one artifact), so a mid-run split was not
  applicable; the deviation is recorded in the run ledger.
